newsitem.title: USA: Ameritech Q1 EPS tops estimates, concerns remain.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech Q1 EPS tops estimates, concerns remain.

text.p: Ameritech Corp beat first quarter earnings estimates, but analysts said Tuesday concerns remain about how the regional Bell operating company will fare in a market with stepped up competition.

"It's a very good quarter," said Bob Venable, an analyst for Robert W. Baird & Co. "It's heartening to see Ameritech report these results, but we still really don't know what's going to happen when competition hits."

Earlier, Ameritech reported first quarter earnings of $0.97 a share versus $0.86 a share last year, an increase of 12.8 percent. According to First Call, the consensus of analysts' estimates was $0.96 a share.
"They beat expectations," said Robert Wilkes, an analyst with Brown Brothers Harriman.
Shares of Ameritech were up 1/4 in afternoon trade at 57-3/8.
Analysts noted that the number of local access lines grew by 3.2 percent over last year to 19.9 million -- a smaller jump than posted in the third and fourth quarters of 1996.
The company said it is focussing on marketing more high-margin services such as call waiting or caller ID along with new lines. Sales of those services grew by 26 percent versus last year.

Ameritech had filed to provide long-distance in Michigan but ran into regulatory issues. The company said it will refile by the end of the month or in early May and hopes to provide long-distance service in all five of its states by the end of the year.
One of the requirements for the regional Bell operating companies' entrance into the lucrative long-distance market is competition in their local areas.
